task_1.title: Werkzeug 2.3 compatibility for testing and URL handling
task_1.description: Update the library so applications can upgrade to Werkzeug 2.3 without breaking Flask test-client session workflows or URL handling. The change preserves runtime compatibility by adapting session cookie round-tripping in test clients, keeping full-URL parsing working in request builders, and maintaining correct fragment encoding when generating URLs with anchors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Werkzeug 2.3 does not break Flask's observable behavior for test-client session management or URL construction. Ensure that session transactions still read and persist session state through the client cookie mechanism, that clients with cookies disabled fail with an appropriate error, and that generated URLs and test request URLs remain correctly parsed and encoded.

expectation.grounded: Flask's testing utilities must remain compatible with Werkzeug 2.3. `FlaskClient.session_transaction()` should operate with the newer Werkzeug cookie handling model as well as the legacy cookie jar behavior, inject the client's existing cookies into the request context, allow session mutation, and write any saved session cookies back to the client. If cookies are disabled for the test client, `session_transaction()` should raise `TypeError`. If the session interface cannot open a session, it should still raise `RuntimeError`. `EnvironBuilder` should continue to accept URL-style request inputs and derive scheme, host, and application root correctly. URL generation with `_anchor` should percent-encode fragment content while preserving standard fragment-safe reserved characters.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to use Werkzeug 2.3 without losing expected Flask behavior. Test-client session edits should still round-trip through cookies, disabled-cookie clients should fail immediately with a clear type error, full request URLs used in testing should still resolve correctly, and generated URL fragments should remain valid and correctly encoded.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress successful `FlaskClient.session_transaction()` behavior when cookies are enabled and a real session is available. Continue to avoid writing cookies when the session interface reports a null session. Preserve support for request inputs that include an explicit scheme and host. Keep fragment encoding compatible with URI rules by not over-encoding reserved characters that are valid within a fragment.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain backward-compatible behavior for normal session and URL workflows while adding Werkzeug 2.3 support. The update should change only the compatibility-sensitive failure mode and encoding behavior needed to keep runtime behavior correct.

behavior: Using `FlaskClient.session_transaction()` with cookies enabled should open the session from a test request context, expose the session object for mutation, and persist the saved session state back into the client's cookies under Werkzeug 2.3.
Calling `FlaskClient.session_transaction()` on a client created with cookies disabled should raise `TypeError` instead of proceeding without cookie support.
If the configured session interface returns no session, `FlaskClient.session_transaction()` should raise `RuntimeError`.
Supplying a full URL to the testing request builder should continue to derive the effective scheme, host, and base URL correctly with Werkzeug 2.3-compatible URL parsing.
When URL generation appends an `_anchor` fragment, the fragment should be percent-encoded while preserving standard reserved characters that are valid in URI fragments.
acceptance_criteria: When an application uses Werkzeug 2.3 and a test client with cookies enabled opens `session_transaction()`, it should be able to modify the session and observe the updated session cookie state on subsequent client requests.
When a test client is created with cookies disabled and `session_transaction()` is invoked, it should raise `TypeError` rather than attempting session access.
When the session backend does not open a session during `session_transaction()`, the call should fail with `RuntimeError`.
When a testing request is created from an absolute URL, the resulting request environment should reflect the intended scheme and host rather than misparsing the URL.

When URL generation includes an anchor containing characters that require encoding alongside reserved fragment delimiters, the resulting URL should encode only the necessary characters and leave valid fragment delimiters intact.
